summary: ITMO University authors run five small open-weight models as read-only repository explorers. Each explorer is a mini-SWE-agent-style loop with ls/find/grep/cat and a 600 s timeout that returns a ranked list of files likely to need changes for an issue. The tasks are 499 SWE-bench Verified-derived issues (12 Python repositories) and 500 issues from 153 repositories in the authors' IssueLoc arm. The reference explorer, GLM-4.7-Flash, leads every localization metric. The others keep about 78-94% of its Hit@3 and 73-92% of its F1 while using 41-88% less time and 84-95% fewer tokens. No frontier model is tested, each model is run once, and downstream repair is not measured.

claims.claim: The highest-quality explorer leads all localization metrics in both evaluation arms
claims.evidence: Tables 2-3 for point estimates. In Table 4, every alternative's Hit@3, R@3 and F1 interval is below zero under instance-level paired bootstrap. Under repository-clustered bootstrap, several SWE-derived Hit@3/F1 gaps include zero (§7.2). The 'reference' is itself a small Flash-class model, and it has the highest error (timeout) rate on the SWE arm (6.6%).

claims.claim: Lower-cost explorers retain about 78-94% of reference Hit@3 and 73-92% of F1 while cutting mean agent time by 41-88% and tokens by 84-95%
claims.evidence: Table 5 matches the abstract (Hit@3 77.9-94.3%, F1 72.6-91.9%, time 41.1-87.5%, tokens 83.9-95.2%). Time includes serving-stack and timeout effects. API-equivalent cost reduction can be much smaller than token reduction (Qwen3-Coder: 83.9% fewer tokens, 8.8% lower API cost on the random arm). One run per model.

claims.claim: The preferred explorer depends on the downstream handoff contract: ranking/coverage for recoverable soft handoffs, F1/exact match for hard file gates
claims.evidence: Model orderings differ between Hit@3, R@3 and F1 (§7.4, §8.1). The link to downstream usefulness is argued from metric definitions. No repair stage consumes either kind of handoff in the study.

claims.claim: Repository exploration can be treated as an independently measurable and budgetable stage of modular coding agents
claims.evidence: Measurability is demonstrated. The benefit of separating the stage is not tested: no end-to-end, fixed-repairer experiment is run (acknowledged as future work). The downstream value is borrowed from the authors' own Loc2Repair paper.

patterns.note: A read-only exploration agent produces a ranked file list from an issue. Models are compared under one fixed interface. There is no comparison against lexical or embedding retrieval, or against no exploration, so the agentic design is not isolated.

Routing exploration to cheaper models costs 4-19 points of Hit@3 (instance-level CIs exclude zero, some repository-clustered CIs do not) and saves 84-95% of tokens. The escalation policy is proposed but not evaluated, and there is no end-to-end effect.
A dedicated explorer stage hands a compact ranked path list to a separate repairer. The handoff itself is never executed or measured.
Time, tokens and API-equivalent cost are reported per explorer. Candidate-count budgets are proposed but not tested.
Explorers are restricted to shell grep/find/cat/sed -n.
Uses a SWE-bench Verified-derived arm with file-level labels, plus the authors' own IssueLoc arm.
Issue localization is framed as the exploration step before any patch. It is not about specification writing.

methodology.sample: 499 SWE-bench Verified tasks (12 repositories, 1.24 gold files on average, about 3,900 paths per snapshot) and 500 IssueLoc tasks (153 repositories, 2.27 gold files, about 614 paths). Gold labels are the files modified by the historical resolving commit after filtering.
methodology.baselines: Explorers are compared relative to the best of the five (GLM-4.7-Flash). There is no non-LLM retrieval baseline, no frontier-model explorer, and no prior localization system (e.g., Agentless, LocAgent).
methodology.models: GLM-4.7-Flash, Gemma-4-E4B-it, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct, Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, served locally via vLLM on 4x RTX 6000 Ada
methodology.variance: Paired percentile bootstrap (10,000 resamples) at instance and repository-cluster level; exact McNemar tests with Holm correction. One run per model, so no run-to-run variance (acknowledged).
methodology.ablations: None. Model is the only variable; prompt, tools and timeout are fixed.
methodology.contamination_controls: Recency of IssueLoc issues; parent-commit snapshots to prevent post-fix leakage. SWE-bench Verified is public and widely trained on (acknowledged).
methodology.languages: SWE-bench arm is Python only; IssueLoc arm languages not reported

standards.peer_review: AgenticDev '26 workshop paper (DOI and ISBN listed)
standards.artifacts: GitHub (mohammad-nour-alawad/IssueLoc-bench): task and label manifests, snapshot builder, evaluator, explorer runners, run outputs and traces, statistics code

biases.detail: Hit@3 and F1 against the historical commit footprint stand in for downstream repair value, which is not measured (acknowledged).
Single run per model. The bootstrap intervals cover instance and repository sampling only.
SWE-bench Verified repositories and fixes are public. IssueLoc relies on recency only.
The SWE arm is all Python, and the IssueLoc language mix is not reported.
A 600 s cap turns long trajectories into zero-credit errors (6.6% for the reference on the SWE arm) and adds timeout penalties to time, which mixes stopping policy with model quality.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Third-party open-weight models only; the authors' own benchmark
coi.funding: Ministry of Economic Development of the Russian Federation
coi.detail: No vendor tie. The authors cite their own Loc2Repair paper for the downstream benefit of localization.

verdict_reason: The design is well controlled: 999 tasks across two arms, a fixed interface, paired and repository-clustered bootstrap, honest reporting where clustering weakens results, and a full artifact release. The caveats are that only small open-weight models are tested, each is run once, there is no retrieval baseline, and nothing downstream is measured. So the 'cheaper explorer' operating points are relative to a small reference, and their effect on actual fixes is unknown.
applicability: For the Java team's harness, this supports a cheaper-model exploration subagent that returns a ranked list of paths for a ticket or spec. Repository access should stay open downstream (soft handoff) rather than restricting the implementer to the predicted files. Expect a real quality drop (4-19 Hit@3 points here, even against a small reference) and keep an escalation path to a stronger model when the candidates fail. Token savings do not always translate into price savings. Nothing here covers Java, cross-repository localization across the 4+ the repositories, or frontier models. KB paper 2608.01507 found that sub-agent-delegated exploration lost accuracy through silent hand-off breakdowns on codebase QA. Measure the handoff on the team's own tickets before adopting.
